topSignals.title: NM Supreme Court unanimously denies Project Jupiter developers' bid to partially reopen the air-quality permit case (ruling published Sept 1).
topSignals.text: Yucca Growth Infrastructure LLC had asked the court to partially vacate its Aug 23 stay and let pre-hearing filings resume; the court said no, keeping the Sept 14 hearing on Bloom's 2.45 GW fuel-cell air permit paused. The underlying dispute — whether NMED can hold the hearing before the project's natural-gas pipeline clears its own regulatory hurdles — is still undecided on the merits. Carries into a new week with no resolution date in sight. Source NM | KRWG | ABQ Journal

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy jumps 8.48% to close at $237.67 on Sept 3, resolving yesterday's flagged price discrepancy.
topSignals.text: Day range $212.12–$238.41. Move continues the AI-infrastructure re-rating theme (Q2 revenue +165.5% YoY to $1.07B, FY2026 guidance raised to $3.9–4.2B) rather than any single news catalyst identified today. Separately, a second law firm (Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman) publicized solicitation for the existing securities class action (Feb 2025–July 2026 class period, China-sourced-scandium allegations); lead-plaintiff deadline remains Sept 28. TradingKey | GlobeNewswire

topSignals.title: Ceres Power confirms H1 2026 interim results for Wed, 23 Sept 2026 (RNS filed Sept 3), resolving yesterday's "date unconfirmed" LCOE flag.
topSignals.text: Notably, Ceres' standard company boilerplate now explicitly names "AI data centres" for the first time (alongside commercial/industrial and green-hydrogen use cases) — a small but real signal of how central the data-center segment has become to Ceres' own positioning since the March 2026 Centrica partnership. LSE RNS

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet for a sixth straight day. No news beyond the already-logged Aug 24 Paris MoU; background unchanged (E3000 G2 platform, 360 MW Tallinn factory, Casale P2X MoU, JNK India MoU).

Topsoe (priority): SOFC/SOEC side quiet — nothing beyond the already-logged Aug 27 H1 2026 results and the May 2026 SOEC-pathway/Herning-hibernation decision. Non-SOFC company news: Topsoe announced Sept 1 a "major breakthrough" in its separate battery-materials business — cobalt-free LNMO cathode cells demonstrating 1,500 charge-discharge cycles at 80% capacity retention (3–5x prior LNMO durability), aimed at automotive EV cells. Different business line from the SOFC/SOEC stack franchise, flagged here only for company-status completeness. Topsoe

Other players: Ceres' updated corporate boilerplate now names AI data centres explicitly — see Top Signal #3. No new stack/cell announcements found today from Bloom, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, or Convion.
Project Jupiter (Oracle/OpenAI, NM): See Top Signal #1 — air permit hearing stays paused, no ruling on the merits yet.

Standing pipeline unchanged: Bloom-AEP 1 GW ($2.65B), Bloom-Brookfield $5B partnership, Bloom-Nebius $2.6B, Bloom-Equinix >100 MW/19 sites, FCEL-Fit Energy up to 380 MW (+$2.4B awarded-capacity option), FCEL's new 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement (logged Sept 3), Ceres-Centrica UK/Europe multi-GW pipeline, FCEL-SDCL up to 450 MW.
Project Jupiter (NM): See Top Signal #1 — Supreme Court denial keeps the stay in place.
FERC RM26-4 large-load interconnection: Unchanged. MISO's tariff filing (Aug 28) is in; reply comments to RTO/ISO show-cause responses remain due Sept 16, 2026.

Rolls-Royce SMR UK GDA: Design Acceptance Confirmation self-target (August 2026) has now passed with no confirmation found — unresolved for a fourth week. Competing on-site baseload timeline benchmark, not SOFC-specific.
Germany EnEfG: Unchanged — draft amendment still pending a Bundestag/Bundesrat floor vote this autumn; no schedule found yet.
Texas ERCOT audit, US ITC 45V/48E, Virginia data-center legislation, EU CADA: unchanged.

McDermott + Doosan Enerbility MOU (Aug 4, background — surfaced in today's search, not new news): Framework to jointly evaluate gas-turbine/generator power projects, explicitly including behind-the-meter generation for data centers. Relevant as another gas-turbine EPC pairing chasing the same load. McDermott

"Gas-plus-nuclear" hybrid for data centers (Victoria, Texas): Engineering, licensing and safety-analysis work advancing on a project pairing GE Vernova 7HA.02 gas turbines with GEH BWRX-300 SMRs; FID targeted 2027. Pitch is a natural-gas bridge to nuclear cutting time-to-power to under 48 months. Directly competes with SOFC's faster-deployment value proposition on the gas-turbine side, and with 2030s SMR timelines on the nuclear side. Power Engineering
Bloom Energy (BE): +8.48% to $237.67 close Sept 3 (day range $212.12–238.41) — see Top Signal #2. Next catalysts: 10-Q Sept 11, securities-suit lead-plaintiff deadline Sept 28, Q3 earnings Oct 27.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Continued post-earnings slide — traded $13.83–14.98 on Sept 3, down further from $17.08 on Sept 1 (was ~$26 pre-Q3-report). Consensus (8 analysts) stays "Buy" with a $22.83 average 12-month price target, i.e. the Street hasn't repriced the long-term thesis despite the post-miss selloff. Annualized production rate target: 100 MW by October 2026.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): H1 2026 interim results date confirmed for Sept 23 — see Top Signal #3. No new pricing beyond the already-logged Aug 26 RFC Power £10M Series A spin-out.
Topsoe: Nothing new on the SOFC/SOEC side; see Stack & Cell Technology for the (non-SOFC) battery-materials news.

lcoe.text: EIA Henry Hub Q3 2026 figure needs a direct-source check — two secondhand citations disagree. Yesterday's digest cited an October-2025-vintage STEO figure of ~$3.91/MMBtu for Q3 2026. A search today surfaced a claim, attributed to the "August 2026 STEO," that Henry Hub stays below $3.00/MMBtu until November 2026 — which doesn't reconcile with the $3.91 figure or with the model's current $4.00–4.30/MMBtu assumption. Both citations are secondhand (news-site paraphrases, not the primary PDF read directly), so treat neither as settled; recommend pulling the current EIA STEO PDF directly before adjusting the model's gas-price assumption. EIA STEO PDF
